notes: One university-layer document (Provost sample-syllabus page) that hosts sample statements from Chicago, UT Austin, Harvard and UMKC units; both coders coded all samples, so alignment was easy. Main disagreements: (1) policy_type, 7 cases: P44 vs P02 for the anti-ban sentence (P44), P39 vs P53 for detector bias (P39), P83 vs UNCOVERED for 'bypass learning objectives' (P83), P91 vs P02/P18 for the writing-support invitation and list (P91, since P18 is about prose vs code), P25 vs P26 for submitting prompts (P25), P31 vs UNCOVERED for capability deterioration (UNCOVERED). (2) unit_stance: B used 'require' for disclosure duties; reset to 'permit' because the field records the position on AI use. (3) actor/phase for tier definitions: set to instructor/before-course. (4) Units found by one coder only were all real and kept: A found 4 (rationale duty, tools poor at self-assessment, prompts own unaided work, data mining), B found 6 (clear-policy rationale, documentation waiver, UM System pointer, two UT Austin sentences, Harvard per-assignment). Where B merged two rules into one unit, A's split was kept.
